requirements.text: WHEN a ticket key is rendered on a surface that does not co-render a status badge, the system shall render a status glyph between the priority glyph and the key text, for any ticket including epics

The system shall map each of the seven ticket statuses (Proposed, Approved, In Progress, Implemented, Rejected, On Hold, Partially Implemented) to exactly one status glyph, with In Progress mapped to the play glyph
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-247 CR §5 Functional + status_svg README default

requirements.text: WHEN a status badge is rendered, the system shall render its status glyph before the status label

WHILE a status badge co-renders with a ticket key on the same surface, the system shall suppress the key-strip status glyph (board cards, swimlane cards, cloud-projected stub, viewer header, viewer attributes, swimlane lane header, list rows)
WHEN the list view renders on desktop, the system shall show a Status column whose cell renders the status badge, and shall omit the STATUS tag from the Attributes cell
WHEN the list view renders on mobile, the system shall present status via the existing lead status tag without a second status rendering
WHEN the pinned-ticket tooltip renders, the system shall show the status glyph on the key strip and shall not render the status badge block
WHEN a quick-search hit carries a status, current-project or cross-project, the system shall render the status glyph on its key strip
IF a ticket status is missing or matches none of the seven statuses, the system shall render no status glyph while the badge label remains unchanged
WHEN a status is flagged invalid, the system shall render the rejected-status glyph with invalid-status colors on the badge
Status glyphs shall render legibly at the 16px strip slot and the 12px badge slot in light and dark themes
The key-strip status glyph shall be aria-hidden with a native title hover tooltip carrying the status name, and the badge label shall remain the accessible name
Status glyphs shall ship as bundled inline components in a map module with no per-icon public URL fetches
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-247 CR §5 Non-Functional resolved by ux-design + STYLING.md SVG Icons

requirements.text: All mapped glyphs shall use a 24x24 viewBox with currentColor strokes of approximately weight 2, normalizing the 64x64 hardcoded-hex source assets
deferred.svg and both fast-forward variants shall remain bundled but unmapped assets, excluded from the status registry
The priority glyph position, the type-icon slot, the epic Zap marker, the worktree marker, badge color tokens, and the CRStatus enum shall remain unchanged
The cross-project search contract extension shall be additive and optional so responses without status degrade to no glyph
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-247 CR Affected Artifacts resolved by ux-design

requirements.text: WHILE pin metadata is not loaded, the pinned-ticket tooltip shall render no status glyph and no status badge block

Status glyph color shall derive from currentColor with the existing data-status to status token foreground mapping mirrored from badge.css; Partially Implemented uses the owner-approved dedicated --status-partial lime token pair (added by MDT-247 user-review round 2), and no other new color tokens

scenarios.title: Quick-search hit shows the status glyph on its key strip
scenarios.given: Given a project with a ticket whose status is In Progress
scenarios.when: When I open quick search and type the ticket key
scenarios.then: Then the hit key strip shows the status glyph between the priority glyph and the key text

scenarios.title: Pin tooltip shows the status glyph and no badge block
scenarios.given: Given a pinned ticket with a known status
scenarios.when: When I hover the pin item
scenarios.then: Then the tooltip key strip shows the status glyph and the status badge block is gone

scenarios.title: Status badge leads with its status glyph
scenarios.given: Given a ticket card on the board
scenarios.then: Then a status glyph appears before the status label

scenarios.title: Key-strip status glyph is suppressed where the badge co-renders
scenarios.given: Given a board ticket card showing the status badge
scenarios.then: Then the key strip shows no status glyph, one status encoding per surface

scenarios.title: Desktop list shows a Status column with the badge cell
scenarios.given: Given the desktop list view with tickets
scenarios.then: Then a Status column shows the status badge per row and the Attributes cell has no STATUS tag

scenarios.title: Mobile list presents status once via the lead tag
scenarios.then: Then status appears exactly once via the lead status tag

scenarios.title: Every ticket status maps to exactly one glyph
scenarios.given: Given tickets in each of the seven ticket statuses
scenarios.when: When a key strip or badge renders
scenarios.then: Then exactly one distinct glyph represents each status, with the play glyph for In Progress

scenarios.title: Cross-project quick-search hit shows the status glyph
scenarios.given: Given another project with a ticket carrying a status
scenarios.when: When a cross-project quick search returns that hit
scenarios.then: Then its key strip shows the status glyph

scenarios.title: Unknown or missing status renders no glyph
scenarios.given: Given a ticket whose status matches none of the seven statuses
scenarios.then: Then no status glyph appears and the badge label stays unchanged

scenarios.title: Invalid status uses the rejected glyph with invalid colors
scenarios.given: Given a ticket flagged with an invalid status
scenarios.then: Then it shows the rejected-status glyph with invalid-status colors

obligations.title: TicketCode renders the status glyph from an explicit status prop only, between priority glyph and key, with native title tooltip
StatusBadge renders its glyph before the label; invalid status maps to the rejected glyph under data-status invalid colors
No badge-co-rendering surface passes the status prop; glyph presence is the suppression mechanism, no suppression boolean exists
Desktop list gains a Status column whose cell is StatusBadge and Attributes omits the STATUS tag; mobile keeps the lead tag as the status column
Pin tooltip drops the badge block and passes metadata status to the strip; unloaded metadata renders no glyph
Cross-project search contract gains additive optional status and both QuickSearch sections pass status to TicketCode
Unknown or missing status renders no glyph anywhere while badge label stays unchanged
Strip glyph sized at the 16px icon slot with data-status foreground colors mirroring badge.css tokens; no new tokens
E2E suite verifies cross-surface behavior: suppression on cards, list column desktop and mobile, graceful absence
Registry maps exactly the 7 CRStatus kebels to normalized 24x24 currentColor glyphs ported from the owner status_svg set and bundled inline; deferred and fast-forwards stay unmapped
obligations.sourceRef: MDT-247 requirements BR-1.2 C4 C5 C6
